title: Alvarez teaches this exactly (De auxiliis II.7): God physically predetermines the will to all its good acts
source_text: XX. Hanc doctrinam accurate & distincte tradit Didacus Alvares in Summa Operis de Auxiliis divinae gratiae libro secundo. Etenim in eo libro capitis septimi Lemma est, Quod Deus praevia motione Voluntati creatae inhaerente eam ad modum causae Physicae moveat, applicet, seu praedeterminet ad omnes actus suos bonos in particulari, salva ipsius libertate. Et in eo capite haec sunt illius verba, Per hanc motionem & applicationem Deus transmutat realiter Voluntatem de uno in aliud, & facit illam de Nolente Volentem. Item, Deus hac actuali motione efficaci ad modum causae Physicae, id est, vere efficienter, praedeterminat hominis Voluntatem ad liberos actus bonos, ut Voluntas a Deo mota per hujusmodi auxilium se libere & infallibiliter determinet ad actum secundum libere producendum.
pass_a_gloss: This doctrine Diego Alvarez delivers accurately and distinctly in the Sum of the Work on the Helps of divine grace in the second book. For in that book the Lemma of the seventh chapter is, That God by a previous motion inhering in the created Will moves, applies, or predetermines it after the manner of a Physical cause to all its good acts in particular, its liberty being safe. And in that chapter these are his words, By this motion and application God really changes the Will from one thing to another, and makes it from Unwilling Willing. Again, God by this actual efficacious motion after the manner of a Physical cause, that is, truly efficiently, predetermines the Will of man to free good acts, that the Will moved by God through help of this kind may determine itself freely and infallibly to producing the second act freely.
pass_b_english: Diego Alvarez sets out this teaching accurately and clearly in the Summa of his work De auxiliis divinae gratiae, book 2. The heading of chapter 7 there reads: 'That God, by a prior motion inhering in the created will, moves, applies, or predetermines it in the manner of a physical cause to all its good acts in particular, without prejudice to its freedom.'

In that chapter he writes: 'By this motion and application God really changes the will from one state to another and makes it willing instead of unwilling.' And again: 'By this actual, efficacious motion, in the manner of a physical cause, that is, truly as an efficient cause, God predetermines man's will to free good acts, so that the will, moved by God through help of this kind, determines itself freely and infallibly to produce its second act freely.'

choices.why: Kept as the Thomist technical term; Le Blanc explains 'physical' as opposed to 'moral', not to 'supernatural'.
